Alex (Acme-Corp): Hey, heads-up — our embeddings cache hit rate tanked yesterday after we switched to batch-based uploads. We see a ton of cache misses even for repeated inputs.
Alex (Acme-Corp): Example: sending same 3 texts in different batch orders yields different cache behavior. 1/3 hits, sometimes 0/3.
Maya (Support): Sorry about that — can you paste a minimal repro or logs? Are you using prefixing or tenancy namespace?
Alex (Acme-Corp): We use `prefix: acme-prod` (set on client side) to avoid collisions across teams. Here's our client flow: we compute key = `prefix + sha256(text)` then call `POST /v1/embeddings` with batch of texts.
Alex (Acme-Corp): Quick pseudo:
```
texts = ["A","B","C"]
keys = [f"acme-prod:{sha256(t)}" for t in texts]
client.embed(texts, cache_keys=keys, batch_size=3, preserve_order=false)
```
Alex (Acme-Corp): When preserve_order=false we see different hits depending on order and client-side batch chunking.
Maya (Support): Thanks. Do you have any server-side request IDs or logs? Any 4xx/5xx?
Alex (Acme-Corp): No 4xx/5xx. Latency normal, but cache misses -> extra compute and bill spike. Billing shows extra embedding tokens billed for same texts.
Maya (Support): Ok forwarding to runtime. @Ethan can you take a look? Suspect cache keying mismatch when batching.
Ethan (Eng: runtime): On it. A few clarifying q's: which model variant and embedding dim? Also are keys hashed on client AND server? The platform expects either a stable client key or a raw input key; double-hashing can cause mismatch.
Alex (Acme-Corp): Model `open-embed-1024-v1` (embedding_dim=1024). We hash on client and pass `cache_key` in metadata. Server only indexes by `cache_key` if provided, otherwise hashes text server-side. We always provide.
Ethan (Eng: runtime): Hmm. Any chance `cache_key` values are being truncated/sanitized? We recently rolled a change where very long metadata fields (>=128 chars) get truncated to 128 to protect persistence layer. That would cause mismatches.
Alex (Acme-Corp): Keys are ~80 chars so not truncated. Also, misses vary by batch order not length.
Priya (ML Eng): Could be batching reordering + nondeterministic mapping of items to cache lookups. We do parallel cache lookups per batch and there was a bug where per-request namespace was read from the first item in the batch only. If your batch contains mixed prefixes (unlikely but maybe), lookup namespace gets set incorrectly.
Maya (Support): Alex — do you ever mix prefixes within same request?
Alex (Acme-Corp): No, always same prefix `acme-prod`.
Ethan (Eng: runtime): Ok stepping through logs. @CacheBot can you pull cache-lookup traces for ts=1792509800..1792509950 for tenant `acme-prod` and model `open-embed-1024-v1`?
CacheBot: Fetching cache traces... returned 24 entries. Attaching sampled trace (id: ct-3872):
```
TRACE ct-3872
request_id: rq-7a9
batch_size: 3
items:
 - key: "acme-prod:3f5a..." -> cache_lookup: MISS -> downstream compute
 - key: "acme-prod:9d1b..." -> cache_lookup: HIT (served)
 - key: "acme-prod:ff12..." -> cache_lookup: MISS -> compute
notes: namespace used: "acme-prod"
```
CacheBot: Another trace ct-3879: namespace used: "acme-prod" for item 1, but namespace: "acme-prod-v2" for subsequent parallel lookup shards.
Ethan (Eng: runtime): Aha. There's a race in the shard-scoped namespace loader. For big batches we start parallel workers and a config refresh could flip the namespace while lookups running, causing mixed-namespace lookups and spurious misses. This would explain order-sensitive behavior.
Alex (Acme-Corp): That seems plausible. We saw pattern around config rollout window last night.
Priya (ML Eng): Also worth checking embedding dim — if a cached vector was stored with older model (dim 1536) and now you query with 1024, you could still get miss/soft-error. But logs show explicit cache_lookup MISS, not dim mismatch errors.
Maya (Support): Can you outline repro steps we can run ourselves? Also our billing team asks for root cause steps.
Ethan (Eng: runtime): Repro plan: 1) Create 3 texts with stable keys (sha256). 2) Send as batch A=[A,B,C] and batch B=[C,B,A] with preserve_order=false and the same cache_key list mapping in same order. 3) Observe cache lookup traces and downstream compute count. 4) Repeat while toggling a config flag to force a config refresh mid-run to mimic rollout.
Ethan (Eng: runtime): Quick script (shell + curl) to reproduce:
```
# generate keys
K1=$(echo -n "A" | sha256sum | cut -d' ' -f1)
K2=$(echo -n "B" | sha256sum | cut -d' ' -f1)
K3=$(echo -n "C" | sha256sum | cut -d' ' -f1)
# send batch 1
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
 -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
 -d '{"model":"open-embed-1024-v1","inputs":["A","B","C"],"cache_keys":["acme-prod:'$K1'","acme-prod:'$K2'","acme-prod:'$K3'"]}'
# send batch 2
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
 -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
 -d '{"model":"open-embed-1024-v1","inputs":["C","B","A"],"cache_keys":["acme-prod:'$K3'","acme-prod:'$K2'","acme-prod:'$K1'"]}'
```
Ethan (Eng: runtime): If you see different numbers of cache_lookup HITs across runs, we can correlate with config refresh logs.
Alex (Acme-Corp): We'll run it in staging and post traces. Also — billing: we were charged for extra compute tokens last night. Any chance those compute events are double-counted when cache shard mis-namespace happens?
Priya (ML Eng): Not double-counted but you are billed for every compute eviction/hit that falls back to model inference. So increased misses -> higher bill. We can provide an itemized invoice for the range.
Maya (Support): I'll file a billing investigation concurrently. @OpsBot can you mark billing review and create a ticket?
OpsBot: Ticket created: BILL-8792 (title: "Acme increased embedding compute due to cache misses"), assigned to Billing-Team.
Ethan (Eng: runtime): Fix plan: hotfix to ensure per-batch namespace is computed once and passed immutably to parallel workers. Also add telemetry to detect mixed-namespace lookups and emit metric `embed.cache.namespace_mismatch`.
Maya (Support): ETA for hotfix?
Ethan (Eng: runtime): I'll push a hotfix to canary in 2 hours, full rollout in 24h pending tests.
Alex (Acme-Corp): Appreciate it. Also can you advise on a short-term workaround?
Priya (ML Eng): Workarounds: 1) set `preserve_order=true` to force single-threaded lookup path (reduces perf but stable); 2) send single-item requests (not ideal); 3) add tenant_id to cache_key and keep keys < 128 chars.
Alex (Acme-Corp): We'll enable preserve_order in staging now.
Maya (Support): Alex, once you run the repro with preserve_order=true and false please paste the traces. We'll use that to validate the hotfix and billing credits.
Alex (Acme-Corp): Running now... staging run attached, looks like preserve_order=true -> 3/3 hits, preserve_order=false -> 1/3 hits.
Alex (Acme-Corp): Repro traces:
```
staging-run-1: preserve_order=true
cache_hits: 3
staging-run-2: preserve_order=false
cache_hits: 1
```
Maya (Support): Great repro, thanks. Escalating to Billing and Eng. We'll follow-up with an interim credit for the compute delta while hotfix rolls out.
Ethan (Eng: runtime): I'll post a follow-up here once canary deploys. Also creating PR to add stricter guards and unit tests.
Ethan (Eng: runtime): PR: github.com/redwood/infra/pull/4521 (adds per-batch namespace binding + metric)
Maya (Support): Closing loop items: support ticket SUP-6211 updated, billing ticket BILL-8792 created, eng PR linked, hotfix scheduled.
Alex (Acme-Corp): Thanks team :rocket:
Ethan (Eng: runtime): Hotfix rolled to canary at 1792512850, metric `embed.cache.namespace_mismatch` dropped to 0. Full rollout in progress.
Maya (Support): Billing offered prorated credit for extra compute during window 1792509600..1792509950. Alex, please confirm you see credit reflected in invoice.
Alex (Acme-Corp): Confirmed — credit applied. Thanks for fast turnaround.
Priya (ML Eng): Will follow-up with a short doc blurb about cache key hygiene and a recommended client snippet for stable key construction.
Maya (Support): Adding doc task to product docs backlog.
Ethan (Eng: runtime): Closing internal action: add integration test covering mixed-batch/parallel worker behavior.
Alex (Acme-Corp): Cheers, closing from our side.
